clue.text: It's done with meal to pour out a drink

indicators.note: pouring something out tips it about, so the words done and meal are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drink is produced by pouring away the remains of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pour out' signals the anagram of DONE and MEAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a familiar soft drink made from lemons, sugar and water.

clue.text: City prostitute lost head going to a city elsewhere

parts.note: LA is the usual abbreviation for Los Angeles

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word for prostitute is dropped

parts.note: whore is a blunt word for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A streetwalker from one city loses her head when moving to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost head' drops the first letter; LA is Los Angeles, and the answer is a city in Pakistan, hence 'elsewhere'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is a major city in Pakistan, hence a city somewhere other than LA.

clue.text: Powerful hit gym exercise

indicators.note: exercising the words works them over, so the letters of hit and gym are reordered

explanation.surface: A punishing gym workout that packs a real punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise' is the anagram signal for HIT and GYM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty is a straightforward synonym of powerful, describing great strength.

clue.text: Mark books in European city

indicators.note: in says the books go inside the name of the city

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
OT is the Old Testament, the usual crossword books

explanation.surface: Someone notes which books are found in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something is to observe or take note of it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Lothario, or Spooner's soles

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of two words, as the Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: lemon sole is a kind of flatfish
Dover sole is another kind of flatfish

explanation.surface: A womaniser compared with a pair of fish fillets.
explanation.walkthrough: Lemon sole and Dover sole are two flatfish; swap their first letters and LEMON DOVER becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer of women, which a passionate romancer of this phrase is.

clue.text: Row of America with old English parliament

parts.note: the Rump Parliament sat in England in the 1640s and 1650s
US abbreviates United States of America

explanation.surface: A quarrel between America and an old English assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rump Parliament was what remained of the Long Parliament after its purge in 1648.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance, much like a row or commotion.

clue.text: Where awkward types may be taken in hospital?

definitions.text: Where awkward types may be taken in hospital?

parts.words: Where awkward types may be taken in hospital
parts.note: read as UN plus TOWARD, a hospital ward for the un- people, while the whole word means awkward or unfortunate

explanation.surface: Asks which ward of a hospital troublesome patients are sent to.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means awkward or unfavourable, and split it looks like a ward in a hospital.

clue.text: Vegetable cuts below standard

indicators.note: in a down clue, below places the cuts under the standard

parts.note: par is the normal standard or level
snips are small cuts made with scissors

explanation.surface: Some cuts fall below an accepted level.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are pale root vegetables related to the carrot.

clue.text: Award by teacher exclaimed as unexpected

indicators.note: exclaimed means the phrase is to be heard said out loud

parts.note: a prize given by a sir, the schoolboy name for a male teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher's prize announcement comes as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR (teacher) and PRIZE (award) spoken together give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a modifier, as in a surprise visit, the word means unforeseen.

clue.text: Rave-up — and it's none too soon

definitions.meaning: a lively party, a riotous good time
said when something ought to have happened already

explanation.definitionFit: A wild party is a fine time, and the idiom for overdue action is the same phrase.

clue.text: One watches violent arrest

indicators.note: a violent arrest throws the letters of arrest around

explanation.surface: Someone looks on while police make a rough arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' signals the anagram of ARREST.
explanation.definitionFit: A starer is a person who gazes fixedly, someone who watches intently.

clue.text: Reserved? It's back in not long ago

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for not long ago

parts.note: recent means happening not long ago

indicators.note: back says the word it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as it

explanation.surface: Asks whether something is booked because it was returned lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the IT of It's; 'in' then places it within the word for not long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticent describes a reserved person who keeps their thoughts to themselves.

clue.text: Twister puts back time in winter

indicators.note: putting back the T moves it from its place in winter to the start

explanation.surface: A tornado turns the clocks back during the cold season.
explanation.walkthrough: Shift the T of WINTER to the front to get the answer; the surface plays on clocks going back in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A twiner is a climbing plant or thing that twists around a support.

clue.text: Other mails sorted to the same degree

indicators.note: sorting mail rearranges it, so the letters of other mails are reordered

explanation.surface: Other post is put in order to a uniform standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted' signals the anagram of OTHER MAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Isothermal means at constant temperature, the degree being one of heat.

clue.text: Tory manifestos for reluctant joiners?

parts.note: CON abbreviates Conservative, the Tory party
scripts are written texts setting out what is to be said

explanation.surface: Asks whether Conservative party programmes are for unwilling recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscripts are drafted into the forces rather than volunteering, so often join unwillingly.

clue.text: Pears, perhaps, lie in a trellis

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of pears and lie might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Fruit trees such as pears lie against a garden trellis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals the anagram of PEARS and LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a lattice on which fruit trees are trained to grow flat.

clue.text: Happy about bill rectified without undue fuss

indicators.note: rectifying a bill corrects it, so its letters are put right in a new order along with fuss

explanation.surface: Someone is content after a bill is corrected without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rectified' signals the anagram of BILL and FUSS, 'without undue' only linking the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Blissful means full of great joy, a stronger synonym of happy.

clue.text: Associates find prisoners are without diplomacy

indicators.note: being without the diplomacy means the prisoners lie outside it

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts
tact is skill in handling people diplomatically

explanation.surface: Associates learn that convicts lack tact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking: the prisoners surround the diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Contacts are people one is connected with, acquaintances or associates.

clue.text: House title conformed to its outline?

indicators.note: conforming reshapes the letters of house and title into a new form

explanation.surface: A property name is shaped to match the building's profile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conformed' signals the anagram of HOUSE and TITLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is a dark shape seen against light, an object's outline.

clue.text: No difficulty in race where cups are available

indicators.note: in places the word for no difficulty inside the race

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
ease means freedom from difficulty

explanation.surface: Winning trophies at a race proved easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race, where trophy cups are won.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea set includes cups, saucers and a teapot, so cups are found there.

clue.text: Element made up of air and mud?

indicators.note: made up of signals the letters of air and mud are mixed together

explanation.surface: Asks whether an element is composed of air and mud, like a primitive theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up of' signals the anagram of AIR and MUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Radium is a radioactive chemical element discovered by the Curies.

clue.text: Trough for a heartless administrator

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word for administrator is removed

parts.note: a manager runs or administers things

explanation.surface: A feeding trough for an unfeeling boss.
explanation.walkthrough: MANAGER has seven letters; removing its middle A leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A manger is a long trough from which cattle or horses feed.

clue.text: Beasts of burden — about time to discover their worth

indicators.note: about places the beasts around the time

parts.note: asses are donkeys, traditional pack animals

explanation.surface: Donkeys' value is assessed in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are things of value, a person's or firm's worth.

clue.text: Retreating with weapons over a long time in Guyana

indicators.note: over means the reversed word lies across the long time, containing it
retreating means going backwards, so the word for with weapons is reversed

parts.note: armed means carrying weapons
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Troops withdrawing over a long campaign in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreating' turns ARMED into DEMRA; 'over' then means it straddles the long time. Demerara is a river and region of Guyana.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a region and river of Guyana, famous for its brown sugar.

clue.text: Taint, ectually!

parts.note: a mangled spelling of actually, which means in fact, with its A turned into E

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something is spoiled, in fact.
explanation.walkthrough: Actually means 'in fact'; spell it as the clue does, with E for A, and in fact becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To infect is to contaminate or taint with disease or corruption.

clue.text: Squeal about sham dealing — that's jolly good

indicators.note: about puts the squeal around the reordered sham

parts.note: to sing is slang for squealing to the police

indicators.note: dealing shuffles like cards, so the letters of sham are rearranged

explanation.surface: An informer exposes a fraud, which is cheered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealing' turns SHAM into MASH; to sing is underworld slang for informing, so a squealer sings.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is British slang for excellent, a cheery equivalent of terrific.

clue.text: Very much like some religious — be silent

indicators.note: some means only part of the word religious is kept, its tail dropped

parts.note: sh is the interjection telling someone to be quiet

explanation.surface: Some devout people would gladly keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' keeps just the opening of religious, dropping GIOUS to leave RELI. The definition is a verb: to like very much.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to enjoy it greatly, to like it very much.

clue.text: Hourglass?

parts.note: an hourglass is an antique timer, a timekeeper of old

explanation.surface: Asks simply what an hourglass is.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is called by this name, and an hourglass is literally an ancient timing device.
